quotes.text: MCP is agent to tool, meaning it connects an agent to external data sources and APIs. A2A is agent to agent connecting agents directly to each other. They're not competitors. They're complementary.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear explanation of how MCP and A2A relate.

quotes.text: The orchestrator does not execute the tasks. It routes work and merges results. That is its only job.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core design rule of the orchestrator-specialist pattern.

quotes.text: Each specialist owns a clearly bounded domain with no overlap. If two agents can do the same thing, merge them or split the domain more cleanly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical fix for routing confusion in multi-agent systems.

quotes.text: A2A isn't about building one super smart agent that knows everything. It's about building a flexible workforce of specialists you can rearrange as your needs change.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the strategic value of agent-to-agent communication.

quotes.text: Map out the handoffs in your existing workflow. Where does information get passed between people or between systems? Those are the spots where agents can take over.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete first step for identifying agent opportunities.

chapters.title: Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry and next steps

takeaways: A2A is an open, vendor-neutral protocol that lets agents discover each other through agent cards and delegate tasks over standard HTTP and JSON-RPC.
In the orchestrator-specialist pattern the orchestrator only routes work and merges results, while each specialist owns a clearly bounded domain.
Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry Agent Service support A2A, so you can prototype one orchestrator with two specialists without custom integration code.
hook: Most AI agents still work in isolation, and wiring them together with custom code quickly becomes a maintenance nightmare. This episode explains the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol in plain English for architects, makers and IT decision makers. You will learn how agent cards, task handoffs and the orchestrator-specialist pattern let agents work as a team in Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry.
